content: 1. Ribavirin, marketed as REBETOL in capsule and oral solution forms, has been shown to cause severe teratogenic effects, including birth defects and fetal death. Therapy with REBETOL must not be initiated until a negative pregnancy test result is confirmed immediately prior to starting treatment. 2. Patients undergoing REBETOL therapy must use at least two reliable forms of contraception and undergo monthly pregnancy testing during treatment and for six months after discontinuation of therapy. Extreme caution is required to prevent pregnancy in female patients and in female partners of male patients. 3. Animal studies have demonstrated significant teratogenic and embryocidal effects of ribavirin at doses as low as one-twentieth of the recommended human dose. These findings underscore the critical need for stringent pregnancy prevention measures. 4. Hemolytic anemia is the primary toxicity associated with ribavirin, occurring in approximately 10% of patients treated with REBETOL in combination with INTRON A during clinical trials. This anemia typically manifests within one to two weeks of therapy initiation. 5. Due to the potential for a significant initial drop in hemoglobin levels, it is recommended to measure hemoglobin or hematocrit levels before starting treatment and at Weeks 2 and 4 of therapy, with more frequent monitoring if clinically indicated. Patients should be followed up as appropriate based on clinical findings. 6. Fatal and nonfatal myocardial infarctions have been reported in patients with ribavirin-induced anemia. Patients should be evaluated for underlying cardiac disease before starting ribavirin therapy. Those with pre-existing cardiac conditions should undergo baseline electrocardiograms and be closely monitored during treatment. 7. If any deterioration in cardiovascular status occurs, ribavirin therapy should be suspended or discontinued. Patients with a history of significant or unstable cardiac disease should not use REBETOL, as drug-induced anemia may exacerbate cardiac conditions. 8. REBETOL and INTRON A or PegIntron therapy should be suspended in patients presenting with signs and symptoms of pancreatitis and permanently discontinued in cases of confirmed pancreatitis. 9. Pulmonary symptoms, including dyspnea, pulmonary infiltrates, pneumonitis, pulmonary hypertension, and pneumonia, have been reported during REBETOL therapy in combination with alpha interferons. Rare cases of fatal pneumonia have also been documented. Sarcoidosis or exacerbation of sarcoidosis has been reported as well. 10. Patients with evidence of pulmonary infiltrates or impaired pulmonary function should be closely monitored, and combination therapy should be discontinued if clinically appropriate. 11. Ribavirin, when used in combination with alpha interferons, has been associated with ophthalmologic disorders, including vision loss, retinopathy (e.g., macular edema, retinal hemorrhages, cotton wool spots), retinal artery or vein thrombosis, optic neuritis, papilledema, and serous retinal detachment. 12. All patients should undergo a baseline eye examination before starting therapy. Those with pre-existing diabetic or hypertensive retinopathy should have periodic ophthalmologic evaluations during treatment. Any patient developing ocular symptoms should receive a prompt and thorough eye examination. 13. Combination therapy with alpha interferons should be discontinued in patients who develop new or worsening ophthalmologic disorders. 14. Patients on PegIntron/REBETOL combination therapy should have hematology and blood chemistry testing performed before treatment initiation and periodically thereafter. In adult clinical trials, complete blood counts (including hemoglobin, neutrophil, and platelet counts) and chemistries (e.g., AST, ALT, bilirubin, uric acid) were measured at Weeks 2, 4, 8, and 12, and then at six-week intervals or more frequently if abnormalities developed. 15. In pediatric patients, the same laboratory parameters were evaluated, with additional hemoglobin assessments at Week 6 of treatment. TSH levels were measured every 12 weeks during therapy. HCV-RNA levels should be monitored periodically during treatment. 16. Dental and periodontal disorders have been reported in patients receiving ribavirin in combination with interferon or peginterferon therapy. Dry mouth associated with long-term treatment may damage teeth and oral mucosa. 17. Patients should be advised to brush their teeth thoroughly twice daily and undergo regular dental examinations. If vomiting occurs, they should rinse their mouth thoroughly afterward to minimize dental damage. 18. Pancytopenia (marked reductions in red blood cells, neutrophils, and platelets) and bone marrow suppression have been reported within 3 to 7 weeks of concomitant administration of pegylated interferon/ribavirin and azathioprine. In a limited number of patients, myelotoxicity was reversible within 4 to 6 weeks upon withdrawal of both therapies and did not recur upon reintroduction of either treatment alone. 19. PegIntron, REBETOL, and azathioprine should be discontinued in cases of pancytopenia, and pegylated interferon/ribavirin should not be reintroduced with concomitant azathioprine. 20. Pediatric use of PegIntron and REBETOL has been associated with growth inhibition. Data from an open-label study in patients aged 3 to 17 years showed that weight and height gains lagged behind normative population data during treatment. Severely inhibited growth velocity (less than the 3rd percentile) was observed in 70% of subjects during therapy. 21. Following treatment, most pediatric patients experienced rebound growth and weight gain. However, long-term follow-up data indicate that combination therapy with PegIntron and REBETOL may result in reduced adult height in some patients. 22. Ribavirin monotherapy is not effective for treating chronic hepatitis C virus infection. REBETOL capsules or oral solution must only be used in combination with INTRON A or PegIntron, as their safety and efficacy have been established only in this context. 23. The safety and efficacy of REBETOL/INTRON A and PegIntron therapy for treating HIV infection, adenovirus, RSV, parainfluenza, or influenza infections have not been established. REBETOL capsules should not be used for these indications. 24. Ribavirin for inhalation has separate labeling, which should be consulted if considering ribavirin inhalation therapy. 25. Significant adverse reactions associated with REBETOL/INTRON A or PegIntron therapy include severe depression and suicidal ideation, hemolytic anemia, bone marrow suppression, autoimmune and infectious disorders, pulmonary dysfunction, pancreatitis, and diabetes. 26. Labeling for INTRON A and PegIntron should be reviewed in full for additional safety information before initiating combination therapy.
